t:
Section 191 of the Agricultural Market Transition Act (7 U.S.C. 7331) is amended—

    (1) in the first sentence of subsection (b), by striking “100 counties, except that not more than 6” and inserting “300 counties, except that not more than 25”; 
    (2) in subsection (c)(2), by inserting before the semicolon the following: “during any calendar year in which a county in which the farm of the producer is located is included in the pilot program”; and 
    (3) in the first sentence of subsection (h), by inserting before the period at the end the following: “, except that the amount of Commodity Credit Corporation funds used to carry out this section shall not exceed, to the maximum extent practicable, $9,000,000 for fiscal year 2001, $15,000,000 for fiscal year 2002, and $2,000,000 for fiscal year 2003”.

fable.w: The section only makes technical amendments to a pilot program: it raises the number of eligible counties, limits producer eligibility to years when the county is in the program, and caps Commodity Credit Corporation funding. The tempting reading is that a pilot program involving producers implies outside involvement, but producers enrolling in a program is not participation in a federal decision. Nothing here requires consultation, comment, hearings, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue.
fable.s: the amount of Commodity Credit Corporation funds used to carry out this section shall not exceed, to the maximum extent practicable, $9,000,000 for fiscal year 2001

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to existing statutory text, specifically changing numerical limits for counties and funding caps. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The changes are legislative directives regarding program parameters, not mechanisms for public participation.
qwen_block.s: Section 191 of the Agricultural Market Transition Act (7 U.S.C. 7331) is amended— (1) in the first sentence of subsection (b), by striking “100 counties, except that not more than 6” and inserting “300 counties, except that not more than 25”; (2) in subsection (c)(2), by inserting before the semicolon the following: “during any calendar year in which a county in which the farm of the producer is located is included in the pilot program”; and (3) in the first sentence of subsection (h), by inserting before the period at the end the following: “, except that the amount of Commodity Credit Corporation funds used to carry out this section shall not exceed, to the maximum extent practicable, $9,000,000 for fiscal year 2001, $15,000,000 for fiscal year 2002, and $2,000,000 for fiscal year 2003”.

opus.w: This amendment only changes how many counties the pilot program can cover, adds a time condition to producer eligibility, and caps Commodity Credit Corporation funding. Producers taking part in a federal pilot program are receiving a benefit, which the definition excludes; they are not taking part in a federal decision. Nothing here requires or allows the government to consult outsiders, hold hearings, set up outside advisory bodies, issue rules, or grant a right to sue.
opus.s: by inserting before the semicolon the following: “during any calendar year in which a county in which the farm of the producer is located is included in the pilot program”
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The text mentions a "pilot program", "the producer" and counties being "included in the pilot program". That sounds like outsiders taking part. But farmers enrolling in a federal pilot program are applying for or receiving a benefit, which the definition excludes. Including a county in the program is not the same as consulting that county.
2. **What the section actually does:** It raises the cap on the number of counties, adds a time condition to producer eligibility, and caps Commodity Credit Corporation funding. It creates no comment period, hearing, outside advisory body, consultation duty, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section amends numerical limits and funding caps for a pilot program but does not establish any process for outside parties to participate in decision-making. There is no mention of public comment, advisory committees, consultation with states or tribes, or any other form of participation as defined. The changes are internal administrative adjustments.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the number of counties in a pilot program implies some form of selection process involving outside parties. However, the text itself only specifies numerical limits and funding caps; it does not describe *how* the counties are selected or who is involved in that selection. There is no mention of public comment, advisory boards, consultation with states, or any other mechanism for outside participation. The changes are purely administrative adjustments to statutory parameters.
